In East Hartford, Willow Brook went out of its banks, inundating parking lots and roadways at Rentschler Field at Pratt & Whitney Stadium.  Roads and buildings also were flooded elsewhere in town, including several homes.

Significant urban flash flooding occurred in Hartford.  The Fire Dept. reported that Homestead Avenue was closed due to flash flooding.  Cars were stuck, with water up to the roofs of the cars.  Amateur radio operators reported that sections of Albany Avenue, Laurel Street, and Farmington Acenue were all closed due to flash flooding. In Vernon, for the second time in two months, swiftly flowing flood waters from the Hockanum River inundated a roadway connecting Hartford Turnpike (Route 30) to the Colonial Corners shopping plaza, a hotel, and a few other businesses.  Over 100 guests at the hotel were stranded, with local officials creating an off-road path onto I-84 to get stranded guests out.

In Bristol, boat rescues occurred at a small condominium complex on Main Street, along the Pequabuck River, which went out of its banks.  Multiple additional roads were flooded due to the Pequabuck River.

A National Weather Service Storm Survey Team has confirmed an EF0 Tornado in Branford, CT. A narrow tornado path of 25 yd. width began near Pine Orchard and Oak Hollow Roads and continued northeast...with uprooted hardwood trees showing evidence of a convergent damage pattern. The damage path widened to 300 yards at the Francis Walsh Intermediate School Field...where several light tower generators were all toppled by straight line winds...while the Eastern 100 yards of this area along Sunset Hill Drive continued to show a convergent damage pattern. The tornado continued on toward the top of Whitting Hill Road...where the path narrowed to about 75 yards and where the most intense damage occurred...where some pine trees in a loop at the top of the road were snapped in two. Wet snow accumulated across Southern New London County, but warning criteria snow was met in consistent fashion just north of the northern boundary of the zone.  There was one report of 6.0 inches at 1 NNE New London, but it was the only report of 6 inches. Stonington only reported 1.2 inches as of 0900. Other coastal locations in New London County like East Lyme, Old Lyme, and Mystic which all reporting under 2 inches by mid morning did not report again.

Amateur Radio reported 9.0 inches in Meriden, 7.0 inches in Cheshire, and 7.0 inches in Wallingford. Cocorahs reported 10.5 inches at 3.1 N Wallingford, 8.0 inches in Yalesville, and 7.8 inches at 2.3 W Southbury.
Trained spotters reported 3.2 inches in Hamden and 3.0 inches at 2 WNW Oxford. The public reported 3.9 inches at 3 WSW Seymour.
Connecticut Department of Highways reported that at 11 AM Local Standard Time, Route 431 was closed at Bone Mill Road in East Haddam, CT due to a downed tree on wires.

Connecticut Department of Highways reported two instances of damage during the late afternoon to evening hours of February 16, 2025. The first instance occurred at 427 PM Local Standard Time as a tree was downed, closing Route 188 between Routes 34 and 344 in Seymour, CT. The second instance involved large tree branches downed on Route 42 in Cheshire, CT between Inverness Court and Candee Road at 818 PM Local Standard Time.

The Meriden ASOS reported 0.54 inches of ice, Broadcast media at Hamden reported 0.25 inches of ice, and a trained spotter reported 0.25 inches of ice at North Haven. Tree branches and wires were reported down in Hamden, with large branches reported down in West Haven. Route 243 was closed between Baldwin  Road and Wepawaug Road because of wires down.   Generally 1 to 2 inches of snow fell before the changeover to freezing rain across the zone.  Trained spotters reported 2.0 inches at 1 NNW North Haven and at 1 ENE North Haven, 2.0 inches at Meriden, and 1.8 inches 2 NW Waterbury. Utility company (Eversource) reported at least 15,400 customers were without power, with nearly 1,500 of those located in Newtown, with nearly 1,200 United Illuminating customers as of 24 hours after the storm. By 42 hours after the storm on the following Monday morning Eversource upped the number to 85,000.

Generally 4 to 5 inches of snow fell across the zone from the mid to late evening and into the early portions of the overnight as far as accumulation goes. Trained spotters reported 5.2 inches in Hamden, 5.0 inches in Seymour, and 3.3 inches in Waterbury. Cocorahs reported 4.0 inches at 2.3 W Southbury and 3.5 inches in Meriden.

A cooperative observer reported 7.0 inches in Guilford. Cocorahs reported 6.5 inches at 2.7 WSW Guilford Center, and 7.0 inches at 1.3 N Madison Center. The public reported 6.5 inches at 3 ENE Branford, 5.8 inches at 2 SSW Guilford, and a trained spotter reported 5.4 inches at 1 SW Branford.

A couple of high wind gusts were recorded by mesonet stations. This included a gust of 65 mph at station XHAM - Hammonasset in Madison at 1023 AM Local Standard Time. Additionally, a gust of 58 mph was recorded by a station in Stony Creek at 1041 AM Local Standard Time.

A Cooperative observer reported 4.7 inches in Guilford. A trained spotter reported 4.4 inches in Madison. Amateur radio reported 3.5 inches at 2 ESE Stratford. The public reported 4.0 inches at 3 ENE Branford and 4.4 inches at 2 NW Madison.
A measured high wind gust of 60 MPH occurred at 823 AM Local Standard Time at a mesonet station in Stony Creek, CT.

Accumulating snow fell during the second half of the evening and into a portion of the overnight. The snow did mix with and change to freezing rain for a time. Trained spotters reported 3.7 inches at 1 SW Branford and 4.0 inches at 1 ENE North Haven, and 5.0 inches in North Haven.

A trained spotter reported 4.0 inches in North Haven, with a Cooperative observer reporting 3.0 inches in Guilford, and Cocorahs reporting 2.2 inches at 2.7 WSW Guilford Center, and 1.8 inches at 1.3 N Madison Center.  Northern portions of the zone reached advisory level criteria, with southern portions of the zone falling short of advisory level criteria.
Cocorahs observers reported 8.0 inches in Durham, 7.0 inches in Higganum, and 6.5 inches at 1.4 W Middlefield. Amateur radio reported 8.0 inches in Chester and 6.5 inches in East Haddam.
A high wind gust was recorded by Mesonet station CT002 Middletown - Rt9nb in Middletown at 1029 AM Local Standard Time.
Cocorahs observers reported 2.7 inches at 1.4 W Middlefield and Durham, and 2.5 inches in Higganum.

Power outages were reported among utility companies. The utility company reported / estimated 0.30 inches of ice at 3 W Higganum with power outages reported. Everclear utility reported thousand of power outages in the Higganum area. Power lines were reported down off Route 154 in Haddam. And based on radar a large swath of the northern half of Northern Middlesex would have experienced around a half inch of ice. 1 to 3 inches of snow fell before the changeover to freezing rain. Due to impacts and radar estimation of QPF while temperatures were at or below freezing, winter storm / ice warning criteria is estimated to have been reached. Trained spotters reported 2.8 at 4 W Cromwell, 2.3 inches at Higganum, 2.0 inches at Middletown, and 1.5 inches in Durham.

An accumulating snow fell during the late evening and into a portion of the overnight across the zone. Cocorahs reported 3.7 inches at 1.4 W Middlefield, 4.0 inches in Durham, and 4.0 inches in Higganum.

Amateur Radio reported 3.0 inches in Durham and 4.5 inches in Middletown.  Cocorahs reported 3.5 inches at 1.4 W Middlefield and 3.0 inches at Higganum. Snowfall totals averaged at advisory level criteria across the zone.

Sub-freezing temperatures ahead of an approaching warm front resulted in a period of accumulating freezing rain for all of northwestern Connecticut during the late afternoon and evening hours on December 28, 2025 into the overnight hours on December 29, 2025. As temperatures rose above freezing, precipitation eventually changed to plain rain. Flat ice accumulations of a light glaze to 0.20 inches occurred which resulted in some slippery travel conditions.
Zone average snowfall of 6.7 inches.
Zone average snowfall of 3.5 inches.

High pressure over the region brought a period of hot and humid conditions to portions of northwestern Connecticut on July 29-30, 2025. Maximum heat index values (feels like temperatures) between 95 and 104 degrees were observed in some areas during the afternoon hours on one or multiple days. On July 30, 2025, a couple of thunderstorms developed ahead of an approaching cold front during the afternoon hours. One of the storms became severe resulting in downed trees and wires.

Hot and humid conditions developed across portions of northwestern Connecticut on July 25, 2025 ahead of a passing cold front. Peak heat index values (feels like temperatures) between 95 and 102 degrees were observed. In addition, scattered showers and thunderstorms developed ahead of the cold front during the afternoon hours with some storms becoming severe downing trees and wires. One tree fell onto an occupied vehicle resulting in an injury (direct).

A ridge of high pressure brought a period of hot and humid conditions across northwestern Connecticut on July 16-17, 2025. Maximum heat index values (feels-like temperatures) between 95 and 102 degrees occurred each afternoon.

Several portions of Route 272 were washed out due to flash flooding between Bruey Road to Route 263 in Goshen. Numerous side roads were also closed including Smith Road, Old Goshen Road, Estey Road and Meekertown Road.
Two houses were evacuated along Preston Mountain Road due to rising flood waters.
A culvert running under train tracks near the Town of Cornwall was washed out by flash flooding.

The Housatonic River at Gaylordsville, Connecticut rose above flood stage during the morning hours on December 18 and peaked at moderate flood stage (maximum height of 10.26 feet) during the early morning hours on December 19 through the afternoon hours on December 19. The river fell below flood stage during the evening hours on December 21. At this height, water reached portions of West Street, Young's Field Road and Spring Street in the Town of New Milford. In addition, US Route 7 at Bridge Street flooded in the Town of New Milford.

The Housatonic River at Stevenson, Connecticut rose above flood stage during the early morning hours on December 18 and peaked at moderate flood stage (maximum height of 16.49 feet) from the late morning hours on December 18 into the overnight hours on December 19. The river fell below flood stage during the morning hours on December 21. At this height, numerous homes in the Maples area along Indian Well Road in the City of Shelton were affected.
